title: A chats resource with correct methods and status codes
problem: chats_api.py has the app, a ChatIn body model and an in-memory store, but no routes. Add create, read, rename (PUT) and delete for chats, with the status codes, headers and error bodies below. Chat titles are unique, ignoring case.
requirements: POST /chats with {"title": str} creates {"id": int, "title": str}: 201, Location: /chats/{id}, the chat as the body. Ids come from _ids and start at 1
GET /chats/{chat_id}: 200 and the chat, or 404 {"detail": "chat not found"}
PUT /chats/{chat_id} with {"title": str}: 200 and the updated chat; 404 as above if it doesn't exist
DELETE /chats/{chat_id}: 204 with an empty body; 404 as above if it doesn't exist
A title already used by another chat, compared case-insensitively, is 409 {"detail": "chat title already taken"} on POST and PUT
A body without title is 422 (FastAPI does this for you)
expectedBehavior: POST {"title": "Family"} -> 201, Location /chats/1, {"id": 1, "title": "Family"}; POST {"title": "family"} -> 409; DELETE /chats/1 -> 204 b''; DELETE /chats/1 again -> 404
edgeCases: Renaming a chat to its own title (even with different case) is 200, not 409: PUT must stay idempotent
A rejected rename leaves the chat unchanged
After DELETE, the title is free again but the id is not reused
Second DELETE of the same chat is 404
A 204 response has no body at all
hints: Conceptual: four routes share two checks, 'does this chat exist?' (404) and 'does another chat have this title?' (409). Write each check once and call it from the routes.

Specific: success codes go in the decorator (status_code=201, 204); Location goes on a `response: Response` parameter; errors are raised, never returned. For PUT, the title check must ignore the chat being renamed.

Implementation: a helper that raises HTTPException(404, ...) or returns chats[chat_id], and a helper ensure_title_free(title, except_id=None) that loops over chats.values() and compares title.casefold() for every chat whose id != except_id.
evaluation: Status codes come from the decorator or HTTPException, not from building responses by hand
The 404 and 409 checks are not copy-pasted into every route
